paper.title: Optimal Online Generalized Linear Regression with Stochastic Noise and Its Application to Heteroscedastic Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic online generalized linear regression (sub-Gaussian noise)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Online regression (prediction with full label feedback), not a bandit problem.
unmapped: Learner predicts labels; regret is cumulative GLM log-likelihood-type loss relative to the true parameter mu*
Feature vectors chosen arbitrarily by environment, ||x_t|| <= A, ||mu*|| <= B
Link phi has derivative in [kappa, K] on [-B,B]
settings.definition_quote: At each round $t \in [T]$, the learner observes a feature vector $\xb_t \in \RR^d$ which is arbitrarily generated by the environment with $\|\xb_t\|_2 \le A$. The environment also generates the true label based on underlying function $f_{\bmu^*}$ parameterized by $\bmu^*$ with $\|\bmu^*\|_2 \le B$ and a stochastic noise $\epsilon_t$, i.e. true label $y_t := f_{\bmu^*}(\xb_t) + \epsilon_t$.

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic online generalized linear regression (Bernstein condition noise)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Online regression (prediction with full label feedback), not a bandit problem.
unmapped: Noise independent zero-mean, |eps_t| <= R a.s., E[eps_t^2] <= sigma^2
Link phi has derivative in [kappa, K]
settings.definition_quote: The noise sequence $\{\epsilon_t\}_{t \in [T]}$ is a sequence of independent zero-mean random variables such that $\forall t \ge 1, \PP\left(|\epsilon_t| \le R\right) = 1, \EE[\epsilon_t^2] \le \sigma^2$.

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic online linear regression with Gaussian noise (lower bound)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Online regression, not a bandit problem.
unmapped: Identity link (linear regression), noise N(0, sigma^2)
settings.definition_quote: Consider the case where $\kappa = K = 1$ in Assumption \ref{cond:activation}. Then the problem degrades to stochastic online linear regression ... the noise sequence ... i.i.d. Gaussian random variables, i.e., $\epsilon_t \sim \cN(0, \sigma^2)$

settings.name_in_paper: Generalized linear bandits with heteroscedastic noise
unmapped: Heteroscedastic noise: independent zero-mean, |eps_t| <= R, E[eps_t^2] <= sigma_t^2 with sigma_t^2 revealed to learner after each round
Learner needs R and the link derivative bounds kappa, K
settings.definition_quote: At each round $t \in [T]$, the agent observes a decision set $\cD_t \subseteq \RR^d$ ... selects an action $\ab_t \in \cD_t$ and observes reward $r_t$ together with a corresponding variance upper bound $\sigma_t^2$. We assume that $r_t = f^*(\ab_t) + \epsilon_t$ ...

source.label: thm:ftrl
source.quote: Set $\lambda = 4A^2K^2/\kappa$ and assume that the noise $\epsilon_t$ satisfies Condition~\ref{cond:noise:1} at all rounds $t\in [T]$, then with probability at least $1 - 2\delta$, the regret of Algorithm \ref{alg:FTRL} for the first $T$ rounds is bounded as follows: \cR^{\stoch}(T) \le 34 \kappa^{-1} \cdot \sigma^2 d \log \frac{4dK^2 + T \kappa^2}{4dK^2} + 8\frac{K^2A^2B^2}{\kappa} + 2\left(\frac{2}{\kappa} + \frac{3\kappa}{K^2}\right) \sigma^2 \log(1 / \delta).

results.notes: Paper's K = k_mu (link derivative upper bound), kappa = c_mu, A = L_feat, B = S. Regret is stochastic regret relative to true mu*. Out-of-scope regression setting. Failure probability 2delta. Algorithm does not use T so anytime.

source.label: coro:1
source.quote: Suppose that $\phi$ is the identical mapping. Set $\lambda = 4A^2$ and assume that Condition \ref{cond:noise:1} holds. With probability at least $1 - 2\delta$, the regret of Algorithm \ref{alg:FTRL} for the first $T$ rounds is bounded as: \cR^{\stoch}(T) \le O\left(\sigma^2d\log T + A^2B^2\right).

results.notes: Linear special case of Theorem 7; delta dependence hidden in O.

symbols.sigma_std: square root of the uniform variance bound E[eps_t^2] <= sigma^2

conditions: |eps_t| <= R a.s., E[eps_t^2] <= sigma^2, independent zero-mean

source.label: thm:ftrl2
source.quote: Set $\lambda = 4A^2K^2/\kappa$ and assume that the noise $\epsilon_t$ satisfy Condition \ref{cond:noise:2} at all rounds $t\in [T]$, then with probability at least $1 - 2\delta$, ... \cR^{\stoch}(T) \le 6 \kappa^{-1} \cdot \sigma^2 d \log \frac{4dK^2 + T \kappa^2}{4dK^2} + 8\frac{K^2A^2B^2}{\kappa} + 2\left(\frac{2}{\kappa} + \frac{5\kappa}{24K^2}\right) R^2 \log(1 / \delta).

results.notes: Paper's sigma is variance bound (not sub-Gaussian proxy), mapped to sigma_std.

conditions: feature vectors are standard basis vectors, each repeated floor(T/d) times

source.label: thm:lower
source.quote: Suppose that the noise sequence $\{\epsilon_t\}_{t \in [T]}$ is a sequence of i.i.d. Gaussian random variables, i.e., $\epsilon_t \sim \cN(0, \sigma^2)$ for all $t \in [T]$. When $T$ is sufficiently large, for any online regression algorithm, there exists $\bmu^* \in \RR^d$ and a sequence of feature vectors $\{\xb_t\}_{t\in [T]}$ such that $\EE[\cR^{\stoch}(T)] \ge \Omega(\sigma^2d \log\left(T / d\right) + B \max_{t \in [T]} \|\xb_t\|_2)$.

results.notes: Quantity is expected stochastic regret (relative to true parameter), recorded as expected_regret. max ||x_t|| mapped to L_feat (unit vectors in construction).

conditions: |eps_t| <= R, E[eps_t^2] <= sigma_t^2, sigma_t^2 revealed after each round

source.quote: Suppose that $\|\btheta^*\|_2 \le 1$ and for all $\ab \in \bigcup_{t \in [T]} \cD_t$, $\|\ab\|_2 \le 1$. Set $\lambda = 4K^2 / \kappa$ and \beta_{t, l} = ... in Algorithm \ref{alg:1}. With probability at least $1 - \delta$, the regret of Algorithm \ref{alg:1} in the first $T$ rounds satisfies that: \regret(T) \le \tilde{O}\left(\frac{K}{\kappa} d \sqrt{\sum_{t = 1}^T\sigma_t^2} + \left(R + K\right) K \cdot \kappa^{-1} \sqrt{dT}\right)

results.notes: Lambda_T here is the sum of revealed variance upper bounds sigma_t^2. Restated as Theorem 28 in appendix. Regret defined through f*(a*_t)-f*(a_t), i.e. pseudo-regret type, but bound holds w.p. 1-delta. Per-round optimizer argmax over D_t of min over layers — computational cost not stated.
